DetectorsKubernetes APIs

5 minutes read

Kubernetes APIs

The kubernetes detector reports API versions that the Kubernetes project says are no longer served, as declared in manifests, Helm chart templates, and kustomizations, and Helm chart dependencies that still point at the retired stable or incubator chart repositories. It is stable: its level is recorded as stable in benchmarks/thresholds.json, and the precision floor is enforced on the public corpus (thirty-six repositories, twenty-nine chosen blind). The evidence required for stable is in Decision 0013. The reasoning for API detection is in Decision 0008.

What it reads

File Declaration
*.yaml, *.yml the top-level apiVersion and kind of each ----separated document, including kind: List dumps (kubectl get -o yaml), when both are literal
Committed helm template output (multi-document YAML whose documents start with # Source: <chart>/templates/<file>) the same pair, read as already-rendered manifests so APIs a Capabilities-guarded template hid become findings; Helm is never run
templates/*.yaml, templates/*.yml in a Helm chart (a directory with Chart.yaml), and any other YAML file that contains {{ and is not helm-template output the same pair, read as text without rendering the template
Chart.yaml each dependencies[] entry with a literal name and repository URL; kubeVersion is still read but not judged
kustomization.yaml, kustomization.yml, Kustomization an inline patch (a block scalar) with its own apiVersion and kind, and a patch target with group, version, and kind

It walks the repository up to eight directories deep (at most 2,000 matching files) and does not follow symbolic links. It skips .git, node_modules, vendor, dist, build, target, .venv, venv, fixtures, __fixtures__, testdata, and a chart's nested charts/. Files over 1 MiB are skipped. Nothing is rendered, built, or applied, and the Kubernetes tools (including Helm) are never run.

What it reports

A declaration whose group, kind, and API version match a rule in registry/kubernetes.json. The rules today are:

API version Kind No longer served as of
extensions/v1beta1 Ingress v1.22
networking.k8s.io/v1beta1 Ingress v1.22
batch/v1beta1 CronJob v1.25
policy/v1beta1 PodSecurityPolicy v1.25
autoscaling/v2beta2 HorizontalPodAutoscaler v1.26

It also reports a Chart.yaml dependency whose repository is one of the retired Helm chart repository URLs:

Repository URL Rule
https://charts.helm.sh/stable, https://kubernetes-charts.storage.googleapis.com stable repository end of life (2020-11-13)
https://charts.helm.sh/incubator, https://kubernetes-charts-incubator.storage.googleapis.com incubator repository end of life (2020-11-13)

Each finding carries its rule's sources, the replacement, migration steps, and suggested verification commands (kubeconform -strict, kubectl apply --dry-run=server, helm dependency update). For removed APIs, the rule's deadline is the date of the release announcement for the release that stopped serving the API; the Kubernetes migration guide names the release but not a date.

What it intentionally does not judge

These produce no finding and are not guessed:

  • values from Helm ({{.Values.apiVersion}}) or from a helper (include, template, tpl, lookup);
  • a declaration inside a Helm block whose condition asks the cluster (.Capabilities), or after such a condition in an if/else chain, or inside define or block. Charts use these to keep a legacy API for old clusters, so reporting the legacy branch would be a false positive;
  • a document with a YAML alias, or a file with any syntax error (nothing from the file is reported, including its valid documents);
  • ownerReferences, CRD names.kind and version names, and non-List nested structures below the top level of a document;
  • an API version outside the vN, vNalphaM, or vNbetaM form;
  • remote or $(VAR) kustomize resources, bases, components, generators, and transformers;
  • Helm .tpl files, NOTES.txt, chart tests/, and kubeVersion in Chart.yaml (it is read but no rule uses it yet);
  • a Chart.yaml dependency whose name, version, or repository is a Helm template action, or whose repository is a Helm alias (@stable): these are listed as unclassified, never guessed;
  • a dependency whose repository URL is not one of the retired URLs above (including Bitnami and other maintained repos).

Known limits and false-positive boundaries

  • Only the five API versions above have rules. An API version the migration guide lists but this registry does not is not reported; the kubernetes-1 importer drafts the others for review.
  • A manifest kept on an old API version on purpose, for example for a cluster that still serves it, is still reported. The rule states what the Kubernetes project says about the API; whether the target cluster is old is for the repository to decide, for example with a baseline.
  • A literal declaration in a Helm template that is only used when a .Values flag is on is reported, because the flag is a repository value and Offing does not evaluate it.
  • The stdout of helm template, when committed (or otherwise present as a file), is judged as manifests. A # Source: …/templates/… header is how Helm marks that output; a ConfigMap or annotation that still contains {{ does not switch the file back to the template reader.
  • Custom resources are never matched: no rule names an API group outside Kubernetes' own.
  • Kubernetes release lines reaching end of life are not judged. The kubernetes-2 importer drafts rules for them, but no detector reads them yet.

Data

The rules are in registry/kubernetes.json and ship in the data bundle. Each links the Kubernetes Deprecated API Migration Guide and the release announcement that dates it. The kubernetes-1 and kubernetes-2 importers read the migration guide and the release history.

Validation

Thirty-six public repositories at pinned commits cover this detector: seven targeted and twenty-nine chosen blind by the rules in Validation (the 2026-10-23 beta walk plus the 2026-11-08 stable expansion). The set includes plain manifests, Helm Chart.yaml dependencies on the retired stable repository, and Kustomize overlays. Every expected finding has a maintainer-review note naming the path and line. Corpus-wide evidence meets every stable count in decision 0013. Offline validate on the Kubernetes bucket reported precision 1 and recall 1 for kubernetes. The hits not reported are the forms this page lists as not judged: references below the top level of a document (a Flagger autoscalerRef), and files under fixtures, testdata, and similar skipped directories (kind: List items are judged).
